He had a magic stick.
But the Monkey King was proud and naughty.
Five hundred years later, a kind monk freed him.
st.c: Today, children all over the world know the Monkey King from books, cartoons and games.

b.title: From Troublemaker to Protector
text: Sun Wukong, the Monkey King, is the star of Journey to the West, a sixteenth-century Chinese novel usually credited to Wu Cheng'en. It remains one of the most beloved stories in Asia.

Born from a stone on a mountaintop, Wukong becomes king of the monkeys and then sets out to find the secret of eternal life. He masters 72 transformations, can travel 108,000 li in a single somersault, and wields a staff that can shrink to the size of a needle.
Power goes to his head. He declares himself 'Great Sage Equal to Heaven', steals heavenly peaches and fights off entire armies of gods, until the Buddha traps him under a mountain.

Five centuries later, the monk Tang Sanzang releases him on condition that he guards the monk on a dangerous pilgrimage to India to collect Buddhist scriptures. A golden band around Wukong's head tightens whenever he disobeys.
Along with Pigsy and Sandy, he battles demons through eighty-one trials.
The story still inspires films, comics and video games, including the hit game Black Myth: Wukong.

q.q: Which sentence best states the main idea?
opts: The Monkey King can change himself into 72 different shapes and forms.
Journey to the West was written by Wu Cheng'en in the sixteenth century.
The video game Black Myth: Wukong has brought him to new audiences.
The rebellious Monkey King is punished, then becomes a pilgrim's protector.
q.why: 第一項涵蓋全文；其他是細節。

q.q: Which of the following is true according to the passage?
opts: A golden band on Wukong's head tightens when he disobeys.
The Buddha frees Wukong after five centuries under a mountain.
Wukong goes to India alone to collect Buddhist scriptures.
The novel was definitely written by Wu Cheng'en in 1900.
q.why: 第 4 段：A golden band around Wukong's head tightens whenever he disobeys。放他出來的是唐三藏；他是保護唐僧去取經；作者「通常認為」是吳承恩，且是十六世紀的小說。

q.q: What is the purpose of paragraph 3?
opts: To describe the powers Wukong learns as a young monkey
To explain why the monk needs Wukong's protection
To show how Wukong's pride leads to his punishment
To introduce the other characters on the journey
q.why: 第 3 段：Power goes to his head——自封齊天大聖、偷蟠桃、大戰天兵，最後被佛祖壓在山下：驕傲導致懲罰。

q.q: In paragraph 4, a “pilgrimage” is ___.
opts: a battle against demons
a journey to a holy place
a punishment from the gods
a royal ceremony
q.why: pilgrimage = 朝聖之旅。

q.q: What does “Power goes to his head” mean?
opts: Great power makes him proud and reckless
He grows wiser as he grows stronger
His head is where all his power comes from
He uses his power only to protect others
q.why: 有了權力就驕傲自大。

q.q: Which modern situation is most like the golden band on Wukong's head?
opts: A prize given to the best student at the end of the year
A long holiday given after a difficult journey
A rule with a clear consequence that keeps someone on track
A special gift from a close friend on your birthday
q.why: 金箍是有後果的約束，幫助有能力但衝動的人守規矩。

tr.en: Sun Wukong, the Monkey King, is the star of Journey to the West, a sixteenth-century Chinese novel usually credited to Wu Cheng'en.
tr.zh: 美猴王孫悟空是《西遊記》的主角，這是一部十六世紀的中國小說，一般認為作者是吳承恩。

tr.en: Born from a stone on a mountaintop, Wukong becomes king of the monkeys and then sets out to find the secret of eternal life.
tr.zh: 悟空從山頂上的一塊石頭裡誕生，成為猴王，接著出發去尋找長生不老的秘密。

tr.en: A golden band around Wukong's head tightens whenever he disobeys.
tr.zh: 每當悟空不聽話，他頭上的金箍就會收緊。

tz: 美猴王孫悟空是《西遊記》的主角；這部十六世紀的中國小說通常被認為是吳承恩所寫，至今仍是亞洲最受喜愛的故事之一。
悟空從山頂的一塊石頭中誕生，成為猴王後，出發去尋找長生不老的祕密。他學會了七十二變，一個筋斗就能翻十萬八千里，手上還有一根可以縮到針那麼小的棒子。
權力沖昏了他的頭。他自封「齊天大聖」，偷吃天上的蟠桃，打退一整支天兵天將，直到佛祖把他壓在一座山下。
五百年後，唐三藏把他放了出來，條件是他要保護這位和尚，踏上前往印度取佛經的危險旅程。悟空頭上的金箍，每當他不聽話時就會收緊。
他和豬八戒、沙悟淨一起，經歷九九八十一難，和妖魔作戰。
這個故事至今仍啟發著電影、漫畫和電玩，包括熱門遊戲《黑神話：悟空》。

ph.ex: The song is credited to a famous singer.
ph.exzh: 這首歌被認為是一位知名歌手的作品。

ph.ex: He set out to find his lost dog.
ph.exzh: 他出發去找走失的狗。

ph.ex: Don't let your success go to your head.
ph.exzh: 別讓成功沖昏了你的頭。

ph.ex: You can borrow it on condition that you return it tomorrow.
ph.exzh: 你可以借，條件是明天還回來。

ph.ex: Along with my sister, I cleaned the house.
ph.exzh: 我和姐姐一起打掃了房子。

st.m: It remains one of the most beloved stories in Asia.
st.mz: 孫悟空是《西遊記》的主角，至今仍是亞洲最受喜愛的故事人物之一。
t: Born from a stone on a mountaintop, Wukong becomes king of the monkeys and then sets out to find the secret of eternal life.
Power goes to his head.
Five centuries later, the monk Tang Sanzang releases him on condition that he guards the monk on a dangerous pilgrimage to India to collect Buddhist scriptures.
Along with Pigsy and Sandy, he battles demons through eighty-one trials.
st.c: The story still inspires films, comics and video games, including the hit game Black Myth: Wukong.

c.title: Why We Love a Rebel Who Learns
text: Few literary characters have proved as durable as Sun Wukong. The Monkey King of Journey to the West, the sixteenth-century Ming novel traditionally attributed to Wu Cheng'en, has leapt from woodblock prints to opera stages, cartoons and blockbuster video games.

His appeal begins with his outrageous abilities: born from stone, he commands 72 transformations, crosses impossible distances in a single cloud somersault and wields a staff that expands or shrinks at will. Yet the novel is less interested in power than in what power does to character.

Intoxicated by his talents, Wukong proclaims himself 'Great Sage Equal to Heaven' and turns the celestial court upside down, until the Buddha pins him beneath a mountain for five hundred years. Freed to escort the monk Tang Sanzang to India in search of scriptures, he is fitted with a golden headband that tightens when he strays — a vivid image of discipline imposed from outside.
Over eighty-one ordeals, the trickster gradually becomes a loyal guardian, his brilliance redirected rather than extinguished.
That arc may explain his staying power. Wukong flatters our rebellious instincts while reassuring us that cleverness, properly harnessed, can serve something larger than oneself.

q.q: Which best captures the writer's argument?
opts: Wukong is popular today mainly because of his spectacular magic powers.
Wukong endures as a brilliant rebel who learns to serve a larger purpose.
Wukong's story shows that rebels must give up their talents to be good.
Journey to the West is mainly a story about the monk, not the monkey.
q.why: 主旨：天才叛逆者學會把才能用在更大的目標。

q.q: In paragraph 4, “ordeals” are ___.
opts: happy celebrations after a long trip
long speeches to the gods
religious books and scrolls
difficult and painful experiences
q.why: ordeals = 磨難。

q.q: What does the writer mean by brilliance “redirected rather than extinguished”?
opts: He keeps his cleverness but uses it for good
He loses his cleverness once he becomes a guardian
His brilliance is controlled only by the golden band
He becomes more mischievous as the journey goes on
q.why: 聰明沒有被消滅，而是被導向正途。

q.q: How does the writer regard Wukong?
opts: With amusement, but no real interest in him
With amusement, and nothing more
With admiration and thoughtful analysis
With complete neutrality throughout
q.why: 作者欣賞角色並深入分析。

q.q: How is the essay organised?
opts: His abilities → his many battles → the ending
Popularity → powers → fall → change → why it appeals
A comparison of the novel and the video game
A plot summary of the whole novel, and nothing more
q.why: 結構如選項所示。

q.q: Which statement would the writer MOST likely agree with?
opts: Clever people should never break any rules at all
Discipline always destroys a person's creativity
Clever rebels should lose their talents before they can be good
Cleverness is valuable when guided toward a larger goal
q.why: 結尾：cleverness, properly harnessed, can serve something larger than oneself。

tz: 很少有文學角色像孫悟空一樣經久不衰。這位出自《西遊記》——一部傳統上認為由吳承恩所寫的十六世紀明代小說——的美猴王，從木刻版畫一路跳上戲曲舞台、卡通和賣座電玩。
他的魅力始於他那些誇張的本領：從石頭中誕生，掌握七十二變，一個騰雲的筋斗就能跨越不可思議的距離，還揮舞著一根能隨意變大縮小的棒子。然而，這部小說感興趣的與其說是力量本身，不如說是力量對一個人品格的影響。
陶醉於自己才能的悟空，自封「齊天大聖」，把天庭攪得天翻地覆，直到佛祖把他壓在山下五百年。他被放出來護送唐三藏前往印度取經時，頭上被戴上一個金箍，只要他偏離正道就會收緊——這是一個「由外而來的紀律」的生動意象。
經過八十一次磨難，這個搗蛋鬼漸漸成為一名忠誠的守護者；他的聰明才智被重新導向，而不是被撲滅。
這段轉變也許正是他歷久不衰的原因。悟空滿足了我們內心叛逆的本能，同時也讓我們安心：只要好好駕馭，聰明才智能為比自己更遠大的目標服務。

ph.ex: These old shoes have proved durable.
ph.exzh: 這雙舊鞋證明很耐穿。

ph.ex: The cat comes and goes at will.
ph.exzh: 這隻貓隨意進出。

ph.ex: The test is less about memory than about thinking.
ph.exzh: 這個考試與其說是考記憶，不如說是考思考。

ph.ex: The puppy turned the living room upside down.
ph.exzh: 小狗把客廳弄得天翻地覆。

ph.ex: They travelled north in search of work.
ph.exzh: 他們往北走去找工作。

ph.ex: He chose to help rather than complain.
ph.exzh: 他選擇幫忙，而不是抱怨。

st.m: Yet the novel is less interested in power than in what power does to character.
st.mz: 《西遊記》在意的不是孫悟空的法力，而是力量如何影響品格：聰明才智用對地方就能成就大事。
t: Intoxicated by his talents, Wukong proclaims himself 'Great Sage Equal to Heaven' and turns the celestial court upside down, until the Buddha pins him beneath a mountain for five hundred years.
Over eighty-one ordeals, the trickster gradually becomes a loyal guardian, his brilliance redirected rather than extinguished.
st.c: Wukong flatters our rebellious instincts while reassuring us that cleverness, properly harnessed, can serve something larger than oneself.

discuss: The Monkey King is very powerful but also proud. Is it good or bad to be very confident? Explain.
The golden headband tightens when Wukong disobeys. What 'headbands' (rules or limits) help people behave well in real life?

topic: Marie Curie: A Life in the Glow
zh: 居禮夫人：兩度諾貝爾獎的科學家
src: Nobel Prize Outreach · Science · The New York Times

a.title: The Scientist Who Won Two Nobel Prizes
text: Marie Curie was born on November 7, 1867, in Warsaw, Poland. She loved to read and study.
At that time, many universities did not let women study. So Marie moved to Paris, France, to go to university.
There she met Pierre Curie, another scientist. They worked together and found two new elements, polonium and radium.
In 1903, she won a Nobel Prize. She was the first woman to win one. In 1911, she won a second Nobel Prize.
During a war, she helped doctors use X-ray machines to find broken bones and save soldiers.
Marie Curie showed the world that girls and women can be great scientists.

q.q: What is this text mainly about?
opts: How X-ray machines helped soldiers
Why women could not study in Poland
How polonium and radium were found
The life and work of Marie Curie
q.why: 全文介紹居禮夫人的一生；其他是細節。

q.q: According to the reading, which is TRUE?
opts: She was the first woman to win a Nobel Prize.
She was born in Paris, France, in 1867.
Marie and Pierre found three new elements together.
She won her second Nobel Prize in 1903.
q.why: 第 4 段：She was the first woman to win one。她生於波蘭華沙；他們發現兩種新元素；第二座諾貝爾獎在 1911 年。

q.q: In paragraph 3, what does "They" in "They worked together" refer to?
opts: two new elements
many universities
Marie and Pierre
women in Poland
q.why: 前一句：There she met Pierre Curie——They 指瑪麗和皮耶兩位科學家。

q.q: In the text, a “scientist” is a person who ___.
opts: teaches students at a university
studies how the natural world works
helps doctors care for people in hospitals
writes books about history and the past

q.q: What does the last sentence want readers to understand?
opts: Only women can win two Nobel Prizes
Women can be great scientists too
Science is easier for women
Marie Curie was the only female scientist
q.why: 最後一段：girls and women can be great scientists。

q.q: A girl says, “Science isn't for girls.” Which fact from the text would best change her mind?
opts: Pierre Curie was also a scientist
Paris has many universities
Marie Curie won two Nobel Prizes
X-ray machines help find broken bones
q.why: 居禮夫人兩度獲得諾貝爾獎，最能證明女性也能成為傑出科學家。

gt.en: At that time, many universities did not let women study.
gt.zh: 在那個時候，許多大學不讓女性就讀。

gt.en: There she met Pierre Curie, another scientist.
gt.zh: 她在那裡遇見了另一位科學家皮耶・居禮。

gt.en: In 1903, she won a Nobel Prize.
gt.zh: 1903 年，她獲得了諾貝爾獎。

gt.en: During a war, she helped doctors use X-ray machines to find broken bones and save soldiers.
gt.zh: 在一場戰爭期間，她幫助醫生使用 X 光機找出骨折的地方，拯救士兵。

tz: 瑪麗・居禮 1867 年 11 月 7 日出生於波蘭的華沙。她很喜歡閱讀和讀書。
在那個時候，許多大學不讓女性就讀。所以瑪麗搬到法國巴黎去上大學。
她在那裡認識了另一位科學家皮耶・居禮。他們一起研究，發現了兩種新元素：釙和鐳。
1903 年，她得到了諾貝爾獎，是第一位得到諾貝爾獎的女性。1911 年，她又得到第二座諾貝爾獎。
在一場戰爭期間，她幫助醫生使用 X 光機找出骨折的地方，救了許多士兵。
瑪麗・居禮讓全世界看到，女孩和女性也能成為偉大的科學家。

ph.ex: She loves to dance.
ph.exzh: 她喜歡跳舞。

ph.ex: My cousin moved to Canada last year.
ph.exzh: 我表哥去年搬到加拿大。

ph.ex: Let's work together on this project.
ph.exzh: 我們一起合作完成這個專題吧。

ph.ex: Many families lost their homes during a war.
ph.exzh: 許多家庭在戰爭期間失去了家園。

st.m: Marie Curie showed the world that girls and women can be great scientists.
st.mz: 居禮夫人向世界證明：女性也能成為偉大的科學家。
t: At that time, many universities did not let women study.
There she met Pierre Curie, another scientist.
In 1903, she won a Nobel Prize.
During a war, she helped doctors use X-ray machines to find broken bones and save soldiers.
st.c: Marie Curie showed the world that girls and women can be great scientists.

b.title: Two Nobel Prizes and a Notebook That Still Glows
text: Maria Skłodowska was born in Warsaw on November 7, 1867. Because women could not attend university in Russian-ruled Poland, she studied in secret before moving to Paris in 1891, where she enrolled at the Sorbonne.
There she met the physicist Pierre Curie, and the couple began investigating the mysterious rays given off by uranium. Marie coined the word 'radioactivity' to describe them.
In 1898 they announced two new elements: polonium, named after her homeland, and radium. Isolating them meant processing tonnes of mineral waste in a leaky shed.

In 1903 Marie became the first woman to receive a Nobel Prize, shared with Pierre and Henri Becquerel. After Pierre died in a street accident in 1906, she took over his professorship and won a second Nobel, in chemistry, in 1911 — still the only person honoured in two different sciences.
During the First World War she equipped vehicles with X-ray machines to help army surgeons.
She died in 1934 from illness linked to years of radiation exposure. Her notebooks remain so radioactive that they are kept in lead-lined boxes.

q.q: Which sentence best states the main idea?
opts: Marie Curie named polonium after her occupied homeland, Poland.
Despite great obstacles, Curie made key discoveries and won two Nobels.
Despite great obstacles, Curie won the very first Nobel Prize ever given.
Marie and Pierre Curie did their research in a cold, leaky shed.
q.why: 第一項涵蓋全文；其他是細節。

q.q: Which of the following is true according to the passage?
opts: Her first Nobel Prize was in chemistry, and she won it alone.
Polonium was named after the city of Paris.
She studied openly at a university in Warsaw before 1891.
Marie, not Pierre, invented the word 'radioactivity'.
q.why: 第 2 段：Marie coined the word 'radioactivity'。第一座獎是和兩人共享的；釙以她的祖國波蘭命名；她在波蘭是偷偷念書的。

q.q: In paragraph 3, what does "them" in "Isolating them meant processing tonnes of mineral waste" refer to?
opts: the mysterious rays
tonnes of mineral waste
polonium and radium
Marie and Pierre
q.why: 前一句：they announced two new elements: polonium … and radium——要分離（isolate）出來的是這兩種元素。

q.q: In paragraph 2, “coined” the word means she ___.
opts: invented the word
measured the rays
discovered the element
published a book
q.why: coin a word = 創造新詞。

q.q: Why are her notebooks kept in lead-lined boxes?
opts: They are still radioactive
They are extremely valuable
They are written in a secret code
They are very old and fragile
q.why: 最後一段：remain so radioactive。

q.q: Which lesson from Curie's life is MOST useful for scientists working with new materials today?
opts: Avoid all new materials because they might be dangerous
Work alone so that nobody else is ever harmed
Keep new discoveries secret until they are proven safe
Study the dangers and use protection, even when excited
q.why: 她因長期接觸輻射而病逝——研究新物質要重視風險與防護。

tr.en: There she met the physicist Pierre Curie, and the couple began investigating the mysterious rays given off by uranium.
tr.zh: 她在那裡遇見了物理學家皮耶・居禮，這對夫妻開始研究鈾所放出的神秘射線。

tr.en: Isolating them meant processing tonnes of mineral waste in a leaky shed.
tr.zh: 要把它們分離出來，就得在一間會漏水的棚子裡處理好幾噸的礦物廢料。

tr.en: During the First World War she equipped vehicles with X-ray machines to help army surgeons.
tr.zh: 第一次世界大戰期間，她在車輛上裝設 X 光機，協助軍醫。

tz: 瑪麗亞・斯克沃多夫斯卡 1867 年 11 月 7 日生於華沙。因為在俄國統治下的波蘭，女性不能上大學，她只好偷偷地讀書，直到 1891 年搬到巴黎，進入索邦大學就讀。
她在那裡認識了物理學家皮耶・居禮，兩人開始研究鈾所發出的神秘射線。瑪麗創造了「放射性」這個詞來描述它們。
1898 年，他們宣布發現兩種新元素：以她的祖國命名的釙，以及鐳。要把它們分離出來，必須在一間會漏水的棚子裡處理好幾噸的礦物廢料。
1903 年，瑪麗成為第一位獲得諾貝爾獎的女性，與皮耶和亨利・貝克勒共享這個獎。皮耶在 1906 年死於一場街頭意外後，她接下了他的教授職位，並在 1911 年獲得第二座諾貝爾獎（化學獎）——至今仍是唯一在兩個不同科學領域獲獎的人。
第一次世界大戰期間，她把 X 光機裝到車輛上，協助軍醫治療傷兵。
她在 1934 年死於與多年暴露在輻射下有關的疾病。她的筆記本至今仍帶有很強的放射性，被保存在內襯鉛板的盒子裡。

ph.ex: They planned the party in secret.
ph.exzh: 他們偷偷地籌備派對。

ph.ex: The flowers give off a sweet smell.
ph.exzh: 這些花散發出甜甜的香味。

ph.ex: The ship was named after the queen.
ph.exzh: 這艘船以女王命名。

ph.ex: She took over the shop from her father.
ph.exzh: 她從父親手中接管了這家店。

ph.ex: Many illnesses are linked to stress.
ph.exzh: 許多疾病和壓力有關。

st.mz: 居禮夫人突破求學限制，發現新元素並兩度獲得諾貝爾獎，最後卻因長期接觸輻射而病逝。
t: There she met the physicist Pierre Curie, and the couple began investigating the mysterious rays given off by uranium.
In 1898 they announced two new elements: polonium, named after her homeland, and radium.
In 1903 Marie became the first woman to receive a Nobel Prize, shared with Pierre and Henri Becquerel.
During the First World War she equipped vehicles with X-ray machines to help army surgeons.
st.c: Her notebooks remain so radioactive that they are kept in lead-lined boxes.

c.title: The Price of Discovery
text: Marie Curie's biography reads like a sequence of barriers overcome. Born Maria Skłodowska in Warsaw on November 7, 1867, she grew up under Russian rule in a society that excluded women from higher education, and studied clandestinely before reaching Paris and the Sorbonne in 1891.

With her husband Pierre, she pursued the strange emissions of uranium, coining the term 'radioactivity' and, in 1898, announcing two new elements: polonium, a pointed tribute to her occupied homeland, and radium. Extracting even tiny quantities required years of gruelling labour in a draughty shed.

Recognition came, though not without resistance. She became the first woman Nobel laureate in 1903, and after Pierre's sudden death she won a second prize, in chemistry, in 1911 — a distinction no one has matched across two sciences. Yet the French press also hounded her over her private life, and a scientific academy rejected her membership.

Her legacy is double-edged. Radioactivity transformed medicine and physics, and during the First World War her mobile X-ray units aided countless wounded soldiers. But the hazards were poorly understood: she died in 1934 of a condition linked to prolonged exposure, and her papers still require protective handling.
Curie's life thus embodies both the brilliance of science and the cost of discovering something before we know how dangerous it is.

q.q: Which best captures the writer's argument?
opts: Curie overcame huge barriers to transform science, at a real personal cost.
Curie's life shows that radioactivity is far too dangerous to study.
Curie overcame huge barriers mainly because Pierre did most of the work for her.
Curie's discoveries were less important than the fame they brought.
q.why: 主旨：突破障礙的成就與未知危險的代價。

q.q: In paragraph 1, “clandestinely” means ___.
opts: proudly
slowly
secretly
carelessly
q.why: clandestinely = 秘密地。

q.q: Why does the writer call naming polonium “a pointed tribute”?
opts: It honoured Pierre, who helped her discover it
It was named after the sharp shape of its crystals
It began as a private joke between the two scientists
It honoured Poland, then occupied and not independent
q.why: 以被佔領的祖國命名——刻意的致敬。

q.q: How does the writer present Curie's legacy?
opts: As entirely positive in every way
As 'double-edged' — beneficial, yet dangerous
As a warning against doing science
As 'double-edged' — famous, but not very useful
q.why: 第四段：Her legacy is double-edged。

q.q: What does the final sentence do?
opts: Introduces her daughter's scientific career
Lists her most important scientific papers
Argues that she deserved a third Nobel Prize
Sums up both sides: brilliance and cost
q.why: 結尾總結光輝與代價。

q.q: A new technology could help many patients but its long-term risks are unknown. Which approach best reflects the lesson of Curie's life?
opts: Stop all research on it immediately and for good
Continue the research, but study and limit the risks
Use it widely at once, because the benefits are clear
Ignore the risks, as Curie herself once did
q.why: 居禮的一生顯示：發現的價值與未知危險並存，需謹慎研究。

tz: 瑪麗・居禮的傳記讀起來就像一連串被克服的障礙。她本名瑪麗亞・斯克沃多夫斯卡，1867 年 11 月 7 日生於華沙，在俄國統治下、一個把女性排除在高等教育之外的社會中長大；她偷偷地求學，直到 1891 年才來到巴黎、進入索邦大學。
她和丈夫皮耶一起研究鈾發出的奇特輻射，創造了「放射性」這個詞，並在 1898 年宣布發現兩種新元素：釙——一個刻意向她被占領的祖國致敬的名字——以及鐳。即使只是提煉出極少的量，也需要在一間透風的棚子裡進行多年艱苦的勞動。
肯定終究到來，但並非沒有阻力。她在 1903 年成為第一位女性諾貝爾獎得主；皮耶驟逝後，她在 1911 年又獲得第二座獎（化學獎）——至今沒有人能在兩個科學領域達到這樣的成就。然而，法國媒體也因她的私生活窮追猛打，一個科學院還拒絕了她的入會申請。
她的遺產是兩面刃。放射性徹底改變了醫學和物理學，第一次世界大戰期間，她的行動 X 光車也幫助了無數受傷的士兵。但當時人們對其危險了解得很少：她在 1934 年死於一種與長期暴露有關的疾病，她的文件至今仍需要防護措施才能處理。
因此，居禮的一生同時體現了科學的光輝，以及在我們還不知道某樣東西有多危險之前就發現它所要付出的代價。

ph.ex: Her diary reads like a novel.
ph.exzh: 她的日記讀起來像一本小說。

ph.ex: The plan worked, though not without problems.
ph.exzh: 這個計畫成功了，但並非沒有問題。

ph.ex: His record is one that no one has matched.
ph.exzh: 他的紀錄至今沒有人比得上。

ph.ex: Reporters hounded the actor over his private life.
ph.exzh: 記者們因為那位演員的私生活不斷騷擾他。

ph.ex: Fame can be a double-edged sword.
ph.exzh: 名氣可能是一把兩面刃。

ph.ex: He trained every day and thus became the fastest runner.
ph.exzh: 他每天訓練，因此成為跑得最快的人。

st.m: Curie's life thus embodies both the brilliance of science and the cost of discovering something before we know how dangerous it is.
st.mz: 居禮夫人的一生同時展現了科學的光輝，以及在還不知道危險時就有所發現的代價。
t: With her husband Pierre, she pursued the strange emissions of uranium, coining the term 'radioactivity' and, in 1898, announcing two new elements: polonium, a pointed tribute to her occupied homeland, and radium.
Recognition came, though not without resistance.
Her legacy is double-edged.
st.c: Curie's life thus embodies both the brilliance of science and the cost of discovering something before we know how dangerous it is.

Her discoveries helped people but also harmed her health. Should scientists keep researching something if they don't yet know whether it is dangerous?
If you could ask Marie Curie one question, what would it be?

topic: Diwali: The Festival of Lights
zh: 排燈節：點亮黑夜的光明節

a.title: A Festival Full of Lights
text: This year, Diwali is on November 8. Diwali is a big festival in India. People also call it the Festival of Lights.
During Diwali, families light many small oil lamps called diyas. They put them in windows and doorways.
People clean their homes and wear new clothes. They draw colourful patterns on the floor with coloured powder.
Families visit each other and share sweets. In the evening, many people watch fireworks.
Diwali celebrates light winning over darkness and good winning over evil.
Many people in other countries celebrate Diwali too, so it is a festival for the whole world.

q.q: What is this text mainly about?
opts: How to make small oil lamps
Why people watch fireworks
Diwali, the Festival of Lights
Coloured powder patterns on the floor
q.why: 全文介紹排燈節；其他是細節。

q.q: According to the reading, which is TRUE?
opts: People put small oil lamps in windows and doorways.
Diwali is a small festival only for people in India.
People draw patterns on the walls with paint.
Families watch fireworks early in the morning.
q.why: 第 2 段：They put them in windows and doorways。排燈節是大節日、世界各地都有人慶祝；圖案用彩色粉末畫在地上；煙火在晚上。

q.q: In paragraph 2, what does "them" in "They put them in windows" refer to?
opts: the families
small oil lamps
colourful patterns
new clothes
q.why: 前一句：families light many small oil lamps called diyas——them 指這些小油燈。

q.q: In the text, “evil” means ___.
opts: something dark
something old
something scary but fun
something very bad
q.why: evil = 邪惡。

q.q: Why do people light lamps during Diwali?
opts: To help people see the fireworks
Because it is very dark in winter
To show light winning over darkness
To decorate their windows for visitors
q.why: 第五段：light winning over darkness。

q.q: Which Taiwanese festival is MOST similar to Diwali in its use of light?
opts: The Dragon Boat Festival
Teachers' Day
Children's Day
The Lantern Festival
q.why: 元宵節也以燈火為核心，與排燈節最相似。

gt.en: Diwali is a big festival in India.
gt.zh: 排燈節是印度的一個大節日。

gt.en: During Diwali, families light many small oil lamps called diyas.
gt.zh: 排燈節期間，家家戶戶都會點亮許多叫做「迪亞」的小油燈。

gt.en: They draw colourful patterns on the floor with coloured powder.
gt.zh: 他們用彩色的粉末在地上畫出繽紛的圖案。

gt.en: In the evening, many people watch fireworks.
gt.zh: 到了晚上，許多人會看煙火。

tz: 今年的排燈節在 11 月 8 日。排燈節是印度的一個重要節日，人們也叫它「光明節」。
在排燈節期間，家家戶戶會點起許多叫做「迪亞（diya）」的小油燈，把它們放在窗邊和門口。
人們會打掃家裡、穿上新衣服，還會用彩色粉末在地上畫出繽紛的圖案。
家人會互相拜訪、分享甜點。到了晚上，很多人會觀賞煙火。
排燈節慶祝的是光明戰勝黑暗、善良戰勝邪惡。
其他國家也有很多人慶祝排燈節，所以它是一個屬於全世界的節日。

ph.ex: We call it the 'cat café'.
ph.exzh: 我們把它叫做「貓咪咖啡館」。

ph.ex: Our families visit each other at New Year.
ph.exzh: 我們兩家過年時會互相拜訪。

ph.ex: Good wins over evil in most fairy tales.
ph.exzh: 在大部分童話裡，善良都會戰勝邪惡。

ph.ex: Children wear new clothes at Lunar New Year.
ph.exzh: 過年時孩子們會穿新衣服。

st.m: Diwali celebrates light winning over darkness and good winning over evil.
st.mz: 排燈節是印度的光明節，慶祝光明戰勝黑暗、善良戰勝邪惡。
t: During Diwali, families light many small oil lamps called diyas.
People clean their homes and wear new clothes.
Families visit each other and share sweets.
st.c: Many people in other countries celebrate Diwali too, so it is a festival for the whole world.

b.title: Lamps Against the Dark
text: Diwali, which falls on November 8 this year, is one of the most important festivals in India, celebrated by Hindus, Sikhs and Jains as well as by communities from Singapore to Britain.

Its name comes from a Sanskrit word meaning 'row of lights'. Families place rows of small clay oil lamps, called diyas, along windows, roofs and doorways, and many cities glow with electric decorations.

Different traditions explain the festival in different ways. In much of northern India, Diwali marks the return of the prince Rama to his kingdom of Ayodhya after defeating the demon king Ravana; people lit lamps to guide him home.

Many families also pray to Lakshmi, the goddess of wealth and good fortune, after cleaning and decorating their homes. Rangoli — bright patterns made from coloured powder, rice or flowers — welcome guests at the door.
The celebrations usually last five days and are filled with family visits, gifts and sweets.
In recent years, some cities, including Delhi, have limited fireworks because of serious air pollution, encouraging quieter, greener ways to celebrate.

q.q: Which sentence best states the main idea?
opts: In northern India, Diwali marks Rama's return to Ayodhya after defeating Ravana.
Families light lamps and pray to Lakshmi, the goddess of wealth and good fortune.
Diwali is a single-night festival in Delhi that is mainly about lighting fireworks.
Diwali, the Festival of Lights, has many meanings and is adapting to modern concerns.
q.why: 第一項涵蓋全文；其他是細節。

q.q: Which of the following is true according to the passage?
opts: Diwali is celebrated only by Hindus who live in India.
The name Diwali comes from a Sanskrit word for 'goddess'.
Some cities have limited fireworks because of air pollution.
The celebrations usually last just one evening each year.
q.why: 第 6 段：some cities, including Delhi, have limited fireworks because of serious air pollution。錫克教、耆那教和海外社群也慶祝；名字意思是「一排燈」；通常持續五天。

q.q: What is the purpose of paragraph 3?
opts: To explain one traditional story behind the festival
To describe how families decorate their homes for guests
To list the countries that celebrate Diwali
To warn readers about fireworks and pollution
q.why: 第 3 段：Different traditions explain the festival in different ways，接著說羅摩王子打敗魔王、返回王國的故事。

q.q: In paragraph 6, “pollution” means ___.
opts: loud noise made only by fireworks
harmful things in the air, water or land
too many people crowded into one place
smoke that comes only from oil lamps
q.why: pollution = 汙染。

q.q: Why have some cities limited fireworks?
opts: Because fireworks are too expensive
Because people no longer celebrate Diwali
Because fireworks scare animals
Because of serious air pollution
q.why: 最後一段：because of serious air pollution。

q.q: A city wants to keep Diwali joyful but cut pollution. Which idea fits the text best?
opts: Cancel all Diwali celebrations in the city completely
Allow unlimited fireworks, but for one night only
More lamps and electric lights, and fewer fireworks
Ban every kind of light during the festival days
q.why: 文章提到城市鼓勵更安靜、更環保的慶祝方式。

tr.en: Families place rows of small clay oil lamps, called diyas, along windows, roofs and doorways, and many cities glow with electric decorations.
tr.zh: 家家戶戶在窗邊、屋頂和門口擺上一排排叫做「迪亞」的小陶土油燈，許多城市也因電燈裝飾而閃閃發亮。

tr.en: Many families also pray to Lakshmi, the goddess of wealth and good fortune, after cleaning and decorating their homes.

tr.en: In recent years, some cities, including Delhi, have limited fireworks because of serious air pollution, encouraging quieter, greener ways to celebrate.

tz: 今年落在 11 月 8 日的排燈節，是印度最重要的節日之一，印度教徒、錫克教徒和耆那教徒都會慶祝，從新加坡到英國的各地社群也會一起過節。
它的名字來自一個意思是「一排燈火」的梵文字。家家戶戶把一排排叫做「迪亞」的小陶製油燈，擺在窗邊、屋頂和門口，許多城市也被電燈裝飾照得發亮。
不同的傳統用不同的方式解釋這個節日。在印度北部的大部分地區，排燈節紀念王子羅摩打敗魔王羅波那後，回到他的王國阿約提亞；人們點燈指引他回家。
許多家庭在打掃和布置好家裡後，也會向財富與好運女神拉克什米祈禱。門口用彩色粉末、米或花朵排成的鮮豔圖案「蘭果麗（rangoli）」，則用來迎接客人。
慶祝活動通常持續五天，充滿了家人間的拜訪、禮物和甜點。
近年來，包括德里在內的一些城市因為嚴重的空氣污染而限制燃放煙火，鼓勵人們用更安靜、更環保的方式慶祝。

st.mz: 排燈節是印度最重要的節日之一，用點燈、拜神與家人團聚來慶祝光明。

c.title: A Festival of Many Meanings
text: Diwali, which in 2026 falls on November 8, is often summarised as India's 'festival of lights', a phrase that captures its spectacle but understates its variety. Celebrated by Hindus, Sikhs and Jains, and by diaspora communities across the globe, it carries different stories for different people.

In northern India it commemorates the homecoming of Rama to Ayodhya after his victory over the demon king Ravana; elsewhere it honours Lakshmi, goddess of prosperity, or marks other religious milestones. What unites these traditions is a shared symbolism: light dispelling darkness, knowledge overcoming ignorance.

The rituals are tangible and communal. Homes are scrubbed and adorned, rows of clay diyas flicker on balconies, and intricate rangoli patterns welcome visitors. Over five days, families exchange sweets and gifts, settle accounts and renew relationships.

Modernity has complicated the picture. Fireworks, long central to the celebrations, now contribute to hazardous smog in cities such as Delhi, prompting bans and debates about whether tradition must bend to public health.
Diwali thus offers a vivid example of how a living festival evolves: its core meaning endures while its practices are continually renegotiated by each generation.

q.q: Which best captures the writer's argument?
opts: Diwali has only one true meaning: the return of Rama to his kingdom.
Diwali is, at heart, mainly a festival of fireworks and celebration.
Diwali's many meanings are slowly being replaced by one modern meaning: shopping.
Diwali's many meanings are united by light; its practices evolve, its core endures.
q.why: 主旨：多元意義以光明象徵相連，做法演變、核心不變。

q.q: In paragraph 1, “diaspora” communities are ___.
opts: religious leaders who guide the celebrations
families who live in northern India
people living outside their ancestral homeland
groups that campaign against fireworks
q.why: diaspora = 海外僑民。

q.q: Why does the writer say the phrase 'festival of lights' “understates its variety”?
opts: The lights used are not actually very bright
It has many different stories and meanings
The festival lasts for only a single night
The festival is mainly about food and sweets
q.why: 第一段：carries different stories for different people。

q.q: How does the writer discuss the fireworks debate?
opts: In a balanced way, as tradition meeting health
As a clear and complete victory for tradition
As proof that big festivals are harmful
Without showing any real interest in it
q.why: 第四段把放煙火的爭議呈現為「傳統」與「公共健康」之間的取捨，語氣平衡。

q.q: What does the final paragraph conclude?
opts: Diwali should stop changing and return to its old form
Fireworks will soon be banned in every Indian city
Only diaspora communities still keep the old traditions
A living festival keeps its core while practices change
q.why: 結尾：core meaning endures while its practices are renegotiated。

q.q: Which change to a Taiwanese festival best fits the writer's idea of a “living festival”?
opts: Stopping the festival completely to protect the air
Keeping every single custom exactly the same forever
Burning less paper money while still honouring ancestors
Using more fireworks than ever while forgetting the ancestors
q.why: 保留核心意義、調整做法，正是作者說的活的節日。

tz: 2026 年落在 11 月 8 日的排燈節，常被概括為印度的「光明節」——這個說法抓住了它的壯觀，卻低估了它的多樣性。印度教徒、錫克教徒、耆那教徒，以及遍布全球的海外僑民社群都會慶祝它，而它對不同的人承載著不同的故事。
在印度北部，它紀念羅摩戰勝魔王羅波那後回到阿約提亞；在其他地方，它敬拜繁榮女神拉克什米，或標記其他宗教上的里程碑。把這些傳統連結在一起的，是共同的象徵：光明驅散黑暗，知識戰勝無知。
這些儀式具體而且充滿群體感。家裡被刷洗、裝飾一新，一排排陶製油燈在陽台上搖曳，精緻的蘭果麗圖案迎接訪客。在五天之中，家人互贈甜點和禮物、結清帳目、重新聯絡感情。
現代生活讓情況變得複雜。長久以來是慶典核心的煙火，如今在德里等城市造成危險的霧霾，引來禁令，也引發一場辯論：傳統是否必須為公共健康讓步？
因此，排燈節生動地說明了一個仍然活著的節日如何演變：它的核心意義持續不變，而它的習俗則不斷被每一個世代重新協商。

ph.ex: The new rule complicates the picture for small shops.
ph.exzh: 新規定讓小店家的情況變得更複雜。

ph.exzh: 把我們連在一起的是對音樂的熱愛。

ph.ex: Holidays are a time to renew relationships.
ph.exzh: 假期是重新聯絡感情的時候。

ph.ex: The school would not bend to the pressure.
ph.exzh: 學校不願向壓力讓步。

ph.ex: Each generation has its own music.
ph.exzh: 每一個世代都有自己的音樂。

st.m: Diwali thus offers a vivid example of how a living festival evolves: its core meaning endures while its practices are continually renegotiated by each generation.
st.mz: 排燈節說明一個活的節日如何演變：核心意義不變，做法則不斷調整。

The rituals are tangible and communal.
Modernity has complicated the picture.

topic: Carl Sagan and the Pale Blue Dot
zh: 卡爾・薩根與「暗淡藍點」
src: NASA · Science · The New York Times

a.title: A Tiny Blue Dot in Space
text: Carl Sagan was born on November 9, 1934, in New York. He loved the stars when he was a child.
He grew up to be a scientist who studied planets.
He also made a famous TV show called Cosmos. It helped millions of people learn about space.
In 1990, a spacecraft called Voyager 1 was very far from home. Sagan asked NASA to turn its camera and take a photo of Earth.
In the photo, Earth looks like a very small blue dot. People call it the Pale Blue Dot.
Sagan said the photo shows that our planet is small and special, so we must take care of it and of each other.

q.q: What is this text mainly about?
opts: How Carl Sagan made the TV show Cosmos in 1980
Carl Sagan and a photo showing how small Earth is
How Voyager 1 travelled so far away from Earth
Why NASA took so many photos of other planets
q.why: 全文以薩根為主，重點是他請 NASA 拍的地球照片與其意義；其他選項只是文中細節。

q.q: According to the reading, which is TRUE?
opts: Sagan took the photo of Earth with his own camera.
Sagan only loved the stars as a child.
Cosmos helped many people learn about space.
Voyager 1 took the photo near Earth.
q.why: 第 3 段：It helped millions of people learn about space。照片是他請 NASA 把太空船的相機轉過來拍的；他長大後成為研究行星的科學家；當時太空船「離家非常遠」。

q.q: In paragraph 3, what does "It" in "It helped millions of people learn about space" refer to?
opts: the TV show Cosmos
the United States
a planet
the spacecraft's camera
q.why: It 往前找：前一句的 a famous TV show called Cosmos——代回去「這個節目幫助數百萬人認識太空」說得通。

q.q: In the text, a “spacecraft” is ___.
opts: a scientist who studies the stars
a photo that was taken in space
a TV show that is about space
a machine that travels in space
q.why: spacecraft = 太空船；Voyager 1 是一艘太空船。

q.q: Why did Sagan think the photo was important?
opts: It proved that Earth is the brightest of the planets
It was the very first photo NASA had ever taken
It showed our small planet, so we should care for it
It helped NASA find new planets around other stars
q.why: 最後一段：our planet is small and special, so we must take care of it and of each other。

q.q: Your class is making a poster about the Pale Blue Dot. Which title fits Sagan's message best?
opts: “One Small Home — Let's Take Care of It”
“Earth: The Biggest Planet of Them All”
“How to Build Your Own Spacecraft”
“Space Is Much Too Far Away to Matter”
q.why: 薩根想傳達地球渺小而珍貴，要彼此照顧；第二個標題最符合。

gt.zh: 他長大後成為一位研究行星的科學家。

gt.en: He also made a famous TV show called Cosmos.

gt.zh: 1990 年，一艘叫做航海家一號的太空船離家非常遙遠。

gt.zh: 薩根請 NASA 把它的相機轉過來，拍一張地球的照片。

tz: 卡爾・薩根 1934 年 11 月 9 日出生於紐約。他小時候就很喜歡星星。
他長大後成為一位研究行星的科學家。
他也製作了一個很有名的電視節目，叫做《宇宙》（Cosmos）。這個節目幫助數百萬人認識太空。
1990 年，一艘名叫航海家 1 號的太空船已經離家非常遙遠。薩根請美國太空總署（NASA）把它的相機轉過來，拍一張地球的照片。
在照片裡，地球看起來像一個非常小的藍色小點。大家把它叫做「暗淡藍點」。
薩根說，這張照片告訴我們：我們的星球又小又特別，所以我們必須好好照顧它，也要好好照顧彼此。

ph.ex: I want to be a teacher when I grow up.

ph.ex: Can you take a photo of us in front of the tree?

ph.ex: My sister takes care of our cat when I am at school.
ph.exzh: 我上學時，姐姐會照顧我們的貓。

ph.ex: Good friends help each other.
ph.exzh: 好朋友會互相幫忙。

st.m: Sagan said the photo shows that our planet is small and special, so we must take care of it and of each other.
st.mz: 卡爾・薩根讓我們從「暗淡藍點」照片看到：地球又小又珍貴，我們要好好照顧它和彼此。

He also made a famous TV show called Cosmos.

In the photo, Earth looks like a very small blue dot.
